faq.title: Everything you need to know
faq.subtitle: Find answers to common questions about 1-2-3 Fuel and comparing fuel prices in Serbia.

q1.question: What is 1-2-3 Fuel?
q1.answer: 1-2-3 Fuel is Serbia's leading fuel price comparison platform. We help you find the cheapest petrol, diesel, and LPG prices across 500+ stations in Serbia, updated in real-time.

q2.question: How often are prices updated?
q2.answer: Our prices are updated every hour based on data from fuel stations across Serbia. We also rely on user reports to ensure accuracy.

q3.question: Is 1-2-3 Fuel free to use?
q3.answer: Yes! 1-2-3 Fuel is completely free for all users. You can compare prices, view the map, and use all features without any cost.

q4.question: How accurate are the fuel prices?
q4.answer: We strive for maximum accuracy by combining official station data with user reports. Prices are typically accurate within the last hour, but we recommend calling ahead for critical purchases.

q5.question: Why do prices vary between stations?
q5.answer: Fuel prices vary based on location, competition, brand pricing strategies, and local taxes. Stations in high-traffic areas or with less competition may have higher prices.

q6.question: Can I report incorrect prices?
q6.answer: Absolutely! If you notice a price discrepancy, please use our 'Report Price' feature or contact us. We verify all reports and update our database accordingly.

q7.question: Does 1-2-3 Fuel have a mobile app?
q7.answer: Our platform is fully responsive and works perfectly on any mobile device. We're also developing dedicated iOS and Android apps for an even better experience.

q8.question: How does the savings calculator work?
q8.answer: Our calculator compares the average fuel price in your area with the cheapest available station. It then calculates your potential savings based on how many liters you plan to fill.

q9.question: Do I need an account to use 1-2-3 Fuel?
q9.answer: No account is required for basic features like viewing prices and using the map. However, creating an account allows you to save favorite stations and receive price alerts.

q10.question: How can I save money on fuel?
q10.answer: The best way to save is to compare prices before filling up. Use our map to find the cheapest station near you, consider filling up during off-peak hours, and maintain your vehicle for better fuel efficiency.

p1.title: Diesel prices rise across Serbia in August 2026
p1.excerpt: Euro diesel prices climbed an average of 1.2% this week, with NIS and OMV leading the increase in Belgrade and Novi Sad.
p1.content: Euro diesel prices across Serbia rose an average of 1.2% in the third week of August 2026, according to data collected from over 500 stations. NIS Petrol and OMV adjusted prices upward in Belgrade and Novi Sad, while Eco maintained the lowest average in the capital at 194 RSD/L. Analysts attribute the rise to higher crude oil prices on global markets and seasonal demand ahead of the holiday weekend. Drivers in central Serbia saw the smallest increases, while southern regions reported slightly larger jumps. We recommend comparing prices on our map before your next fill-up.

p2.title: NIS Petrol announces mid-month price adjustment
p2.excerpt: Serbia's largest fuel retailer updated diesel and petrol prices at 312 stations nationwide, effective immediately.
p2.content: NIS Petrol, Serbia's largest fuel retailer, rolled out a mid-month price adjustment affecting all 312 of its stations. Euro diesel now averages 195 RSD/L nationally, up 0.5 RSD from last week. BMB 95 petrol saw a smaller increase of 0.3 RSD/L. The company cited international benchmark prices and exchange rate fluctuations as primary drivers. Loyalty card holders may still access discounted rates at select locations.

p3.title: LPG prices remain stable through summer 2026
p3.excerpt: Autogas prices hold steady at around 85 RSD/L as demand peaks during the vacation season across Serbia.
p3.content: LPG (autogas) prices have remained remarkably stable throughout the summer of 2026, hovering around 85 RSD/L at most stations. Despite increased demand from vacation travelers, supply has kept pace and competition among retailers has prevented significant price hikes. Eco and Petrol offer the most competitive LPG rates in Belgrade, while rural stations tend to charge 2–3 RSD/L more. If you drive an LPG-converted vehicle, now is a good time to fill up before potential autumn adjustments.

p4.title: Best time to fill up in Belgrade this month
p4.excerpt: Our data shows Tuesday and Wednesday mornings offer the lowest average fuel prices in the Belgrade area.
p4.content: Analysis of six months of price data reveals that Tuesday and Wednesday mornings between 6–9 AM consistently show the lowest average fuel prices in Belgrade. Prices tend to rise on Fridays and Saturdays as weekend travel demand increases. Stations near highway exits charge 3–5 RSD/L more than those in residential neighborhoods. Using our savings calculator, a driver filling 50 liters on a Tuesday instead of a Saturday saves an average of 150 RSD per month.

p5.title: OMV vs MOL: which brand is cheaper in 2026?
p5.excerpt: We compared prices at 156 OMV and MOL stations — here's what we found for diesel and petrol drivers.
p5.content: Our comparison of 156 OMV and MOL stations across Serbia shows MOL averaging 0.8 RSD/L cheaper for Euro diesel, while OMV offers slightly lower BMB 95 petrol prices in urban areas. OMV stations are more numerous in Belgrade (89 vs 67 MOL locations), giving drivers more choice. Both brands update prices on similar schedules, typically mid-week. For maximum savings, check our live map rather than relying on brand loyalty alone.

p6.title: What the 2026 excise tax changes mean for fuel prices
p6.excerpt: New excise duty adjustments could add 2–4 RSD/L to diesel and petrol prices starting September 2026.
p6.content: The Serbian government's planned excise tax adjustments for September 2026 are expected to add 2–4 RSD/L to both diesel and petrol prices at the pump. The Ministry of Finance confirmed the changes apply to all fuel categories including LPG. Retailers have indicated they will pass the full increase to consumers within the first week of September. Drivers planning long trips should consider filling up before the end of August to avoid the price bump.

p7.title: Eco stations consistently offer lowest diesel prices
p7.excerpt: For the third month running, Eco leads our price rankings with an average diesel price of 194 RSD/L.
p7.content: Eco has maintained the lowest average Euro diesel price in Serbia for the third consecutive month, at 194 RSD/L. With 45 stations primarily in Belgrade and central Serbia, Eco competes aggressively on price rather than network size. Their stations are often located slightly off main roads, making them ideal for drivers who plan ahead. Note that Eco stations may have shorter opening hours compared to major brands.

p8.title: 10 driving tips to cut your fuel bill this year
p8.excerpt: Simple habits like steady speeds and proper tire pressure can reduce fuel consumption by up to 15%.
p8.content: Beyond finding the cheapest station, how you drive has a huge impact on fuel costs. Maintaining steady speeds between 80–100 km/h on highways, keeping tires properly inflated, removing excess weight, and avoiding aggressive acceleration can reduce fuel consumption by up to 15%. Using air conditioning sparingly and combining errands into one trip also helps. Pair these habits with our price comparison tools and you could save over 5,000 RSD per year on fuel.
